rationale: unit:shared.give starts with the observable behavior and now explicitly locates ownership modes on references, never on objects. Reference carries mode and target while Object carries class and fields. Its table matches lean:Shared/Step:Give: move requires unique resolution and Take, returns the identical target with unique mode and clears the final slot; copy requires shared resolution and an already-shared final occurrence and leaves the state equal; promote requires shared resolution and Promote, returns a shared owner of the same target and changes only the final stored unique reference to shared. Resolve and Mode.join propagate a shared reference through every subsequent projection. The Take and Promote constructors retain all surrounding list segments, object identities, class/field names and counter. Sharing a container leaves its fields' reference modes untouched; later shared access to a unique final reference changes only that reference. extra:reviews/repair-2026-10-24/sharing-decision.md now records the user's explicit confirmation of that field-reference update and clarification of path-based access, resolving the earlier provisional design ambiguity. The local Compatible invariant excludes a unique stored reference plus another incoming owner; the note correctly distinguishes that sufficient local representation condition from the path-level requirement. The separately inspected WellFormed.path_mode_exclusive statement establishes the requested absence of both unique and shared root paths to the same target. The Given embedding is not used to justify the newly added sharing behavior. This new comparison intentionally supersedes the earlier inconclusive decision while preserving its historical diagnosis.
